notes: Off protected +12V. ~13mA load including the divider, ~90mW. Decouples DAC full scale from the rack's +/-5% +5V rail. TOLERANCE IS A BENCH TASK, NOT A SPEC TASK: worst case spans 0.66V against a ~0.55V window and no nominal value fits on paper, but this is one unit with a TO-92 part, two through-hole resistors and a voltmeter. E7 measures where the DAC's top codes start compressing against AVDD and selects R2 from that - *** BUT NOT BELOW 5.00V, *** because the DAC8568's C grade is specified only for AVDD 5.0-5.5V. *** THE MANUFACTURER FIELD SAYS 'multiple' AND THAT IS DANGEROUS HERE. *** TI's SLCS144E gives minimum output current to maintain regulation as 1.5 typ / 2.5 MAX mA with Io 2.5-100mA - NOT the full LM317's 10mA - while ST's LM317L gives 3.5 typ / 5 MAX mA [ds ST-LM317L-DS2168-REV7.pdf p.7], so 5mA is the worst case to size any bleeder against. The classic Z suffix is an ST/ON TO-92 marking rather than a TI orderable; TI's document covers the LP package. A BLEEDER SIZED FOR TI'S 2.5mA UNDER-LOADS ST'S PART. Either name the manufacturer or size for the worst case across candidates. The ~13mA load clears every reading, so nothing is broken today - the hazard is a future reader trimming the divider current. Reference 1.20/1.25/1.30V confirms the +/-4% claim; line regulation 0.01%/V typ, 0.02%/V max at 25degC on TI's (0.04%/V max on ST's [p.7]); output noise 30uV PER VOLT of output over 10Hz-10kHz, so ~150uV RMS at 5.21V; ripple rejection 65dB typ, rising to 66 min / 80 typ WITH a 10uF cap on ADJUSTMENT - which C-REG-ADJ already fits. PROPOSED: ST LM317LZ, LCSC C5267874. MAP ITS PINS BY NAME: ST numbers the TO-92 1 = ADJ, 2 = IN, 3 = OUT and draws them in the physical order 1-3-2 [ds ST-LM317L-DS2168-REV7.pdf p.4]

One per branch: +12V analog, +12V umbilical, -12V, +5V. Chosen on ONE criterion - it is the only >=1A 600R 1206 part found whose datasheet publishes an IMPEDANCE-UNDER-DC-BIAS curve (traces at 0 / 250 / 500 / 1000 / 1500 mA). Off the drawing: Z@100MHz 600 nominal / 450 min / 750 max, DCR 0.080 ohm max, rated 1500 mA, 3.20 x 1.60 x 1.10 mm, -40 to +125degC including self-heating. *** A BEAD'S CURRENT RATING IS THERMAL, NOT MAGNETIC, so it says nothing about saturation *** - read the bias curve instead. At 100 MHz this part gives ~614 ohm at 0 A, ~431 at 250 mA, ~157 at 500 mA, ~72 at 1000 mA and ~51 at its RATED 1500 mA. Doubling the rating does not help: a 3000 mA twin in the same package reads ~145 ohm at 500 mA, slightly WORSE, for 0.02 ohm more DCR. PER BRANCH: FB4 (+5V, mA), FB3 (-12V, 10-20mA) and FB1 (+12V analog, ~45mA) all sit on the flat part and get 580-614 ohm, essentially the nameplate. *** FB2 CARRIES THE UMBILICAL AT figures.yaml umbilical-current AND GETS ROUGHLY HALF THAT *** - ~280-310 ohm, falling to ~245-275 ohm at the module total. No 1206 600R bead of any rating fixes it; bias shifts the impedance peak UP IN FREQUENCY, so the bead does not die, its useful band slides off 100 MHz. EITHER restate FB2's requirement at its real operating current OR make FB2 a physically larger part. IR drop at 0.080 ohm max is 28.7 mV at the umbilical current (10.3 mW), 31.4 mV at the 392 mA module total, 3.6 mV at 45 mA. SECOND SOURCE: Murata BLM31PG601SN1L is an electrical twin and far better stocked, but its PDF carries no DC-bias curve either - that data lives only in SimSurfing - so it can be an alternate flagged 'bias assumed, not documented', never the characterised part. STOCK: the Laird part is out at LCSC (C2441375, 0). The named Murata twin BLM31PG601SN1L (LCSC C16902) is rated 1500 mA to 85 C and 1000 mA at 125 C [ds MURATA-BLM31-SN1-REFERENCE-SPEC-JENF243A-0006.pdf p.1] - fine at the module's currents - and publishes no DC-bias curve

description: Entry bulk capacitance downstream of each bead
notes: NOT 47uF on every rail. The +12V branch carries the LM317's divider, the DAC and the comparator, about 22mA against -12V's 10mA - so at 47uF each it collapses 2.2x faster and every rack power-down leaves the op-amps with V+ near 0 and V- at -6 to -8V for ~30ms, pulling all six jacks toward the surviving negative rail. 100uF on +12V balances the decay. 10-100uF per rail per ADR 0004; NOT the strip capacitance, which belongs at the load and is C-STRIP-BULK
